data.name: Help.Sections.UserGuide.Paragraph1
data.value: DOT (Document Optimizer Tool) is desktop software designed to automate repetitive processes in documents and optimize them to eliminate rework.

data.name: Help.Sections.UserGuide.Paragraph2
data.value: The main objectives of this tool are to increase productivity by eliminating rework and reducing errors. In way to be practical, flexible, and fast with scale.

data.name: Help.Sections.UserGuide.Paragraph3
data.value: To do this, it has three main systems: Markup, Editor, and Translator; which, respectively, applies marks and rewrites terms on a scale, applies editing routines that are flexible to user needs.

data.name: Help.Sections.UserGuide.Paragraph4
data.value: The systems can handle up to 100 documents per processing and can be configured to work with up to 5 documents simultaneously for faster processing.

data.name: Help.Sections.UserGuide.SettingsLink
data.value: - (Settings) See more about simultaneous processing here.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowToUse.Paragraph1
data.value: To begin with, all systems are similar. In the application header, we have all DOT systems, in the lower right corner, the settings button with all system notifications and, in the lower left corner, a button to add files. Files can be of various types, but each system has its own specifications.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowToUse.Paragraph2
data.value: The Markup system, in the markup function, supports: PDF, Doc(x), Xls(x), and Ppt(x); in the rewriting function: PDF and Doc(x). The Editor accepts: PDF and Doc(x). Finally, the Translator supports: PDF, Doc(x), Xls(x), and Ppt(x).

data.name: Help.Sections.HowToUse.Paragraph3
data.value: Now each page will have its own individual characteristics, but in general, on the home page of the system in question, there should be three boxes in the center which you can configure by creating editing routines or a table of marks/rewrites.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowToUse.Paragraph4
data.value: By selecting a file in the lower left button or dragging and dropping, you will have access to the system sections. You can use these to configure the system, but also to apply editing routines or a table of marks/rewrites.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowToUse.EditorLink

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Intro
data.value: In general, all systems have at least six processing steps: conversion, extraction, fix, processing, optimization, and saving.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step1.Title
data.value: 1. Conversion: All binary files (PDF, Doc, xls, and ppt) are converted to an XML file (Docx, Xlsx, and Pptx).

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step1.Description
data.value: This makes them easier to read and allows you to read the file without changing its structure.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Note1
data.value: This conversion is performed using the Office 365 COM system, so you must need to have it installed to process files that need to be converted (PDF, Doc, xls, and ppt).

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step2.Title
data.value: 2. Extraction: The data in the file is read as a Zip file and all subfiles are listed and exported to a temporary directory for use in the next steps.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step2.Description
data.value: This also allows the original file to remain free for user manipulation.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step3.Title
data.value: 3. Fix: Here, the document structure is defragmented.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step3.Description
data.value: This step is important to ensure that texts are read correctly. An example of fragmentation is as if the text were cut as: 'a/b/ /c/d'; the system then identifies patterns in the structure and corrects it to 'ab cd'.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step4.Title
data.value: 4. Processing: This step will vary between systems, as each has its own functions and way of handling documents.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step4.Description
data.value: The important thing is that your previously defined settings are applied here.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step5.Title
data.value: 5. Optimization: Here, the file is processed to avoid errors, and apply all marks.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step5.Description
data.value: This ensures that everything will be properly adjusted for the saving step.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step6.Title
data.value: 6. Saving: Finally, the files in the temporary directory are recompiled into a single file (Docx, Xlsx, or Pptx) and then saved.

data.name: Help.Sections.HowSystemsWork.Step6.Description
data.value: Saved formats may be Docx, Xlsx, or Pptx depending on the original files.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Overview.Paragraph1
data.value: The Markup system was developed with the aim of reducing document review time through large-scale text optimizations and adjustments. For this purpose, two functions were created: marker and rewrite.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Marker.Paragraph1
data.value: The marker function was designed to assist in reviewing terms in the body of a document. For example: you have a list of technical terms and need to check if they have been applied correctly. You can pass this list to the system and it will highlight them in red to facilitate review.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Marker.Paragraph2
data.value: Another frequent use case is when there are technical terms that are always wrong and you already know what they are. You can configure the tool to always flag them and replace them manually.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Marker.HowToSetup
data.value: How to set up a marker?

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Marker.SetupDescription
data.value: To begin, you need to create a table of marks (table of terms). You can create one in the create/vocabulary section of the Markup page, where you can create it manually or using a CSV file (if you have an Excel file, just save it as a CSV file).

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Marker.FileLimitNote
data.value: There is no limit to the number of marks, but the more there are, the longer it will take to process the document. The only limitation is in the file structure, which must follow the logic below:

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Marker.ColumnNote
data.value: If you have a file with multiple columns, each column will be transformed into a marker. Note: If two columns have the same name or are duplicated, only the last one will be valid.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Marker.ManualCreate
data.value: However, if you are creating it manually, when you click on the create button, you will be directed to a section with an empty table on the left. At the top, you will find the name of your marker and a text filter; in the center are the listed terms.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Marker.ManualCreateNote
data.value: To add terms, simply click on the add button on the left side and an editable field will be inserted. To save the marker, you need to define the name of the table and add at least one term.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Marker.HowToApply
data.value: How to apply a marker? The application is simple: just select one or more documents and go to the process section, then click on process, choose the marker and where it will be saved. Once all documents have been processed, you will be notified.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Rewrite.Paragraph1
data.value: The rewrite function was designed to optimize text in order to reduce revision time and text errors. For example: you have technical terms that are always translated incorrectly, so to automate this, you can configure the tool to replace the term whenever it finds it.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Rewrite.Paragraph2
data.value: Another use case is for optimizing translations that do not support glossaries. You can configure the tool with technical terms that are not translated correctly, then it will optimize the document and when it is translated, the terms will be correct.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Rewrite.HowToSetup
data.value: How to set up a glossary?

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Rewrite.SetupDescription
data.value: In this function, the table with pairs is called a glossary (it has two columns) and to use the system you need to create one. Similar to the previous function, just click on the create button in the create/vocabulary section of the Markup, where you can create it manually or using a CSV file (if you have an Excel file, just save it as a CSV file).

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Rewrite.FileLimitNote
data.value: There is no limit to the number of pairs, but the more there are, the longer it will take to process the document. The only limitation is in the file structure, which must follow the logic below:

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Rewrite.ColumnsPermutationNote
data.value: If you have a file with multiple columns, the columns will be permuted resulting in all possible pairs of columns.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Rewrite.ManualCreateNote
data.value: If you choose to create the glossary manually, the logic of the last function remains the same. The main difference is that now, instead of a line with only one term, there is a line containing a pair of terms, and just like before, to save it, you need at least one term and the table must have a name.

data.name: Help.Sections.Markup.Rewrite.HowToEditApply
data.value: To apply is simple: just select one or more documents and go to the process section, then click on process, choose the glossary and where it will be saved. Once all documents have been processed, you will be notified.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Overview.Paragraph1
data.value: The Editor system was built with the aim of automating repetitive editing tasks. To this end, it has several functions to meet user demands.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Overview.Paragraph2
data.value: For now, there are two main functions and two more that are in development: rewrite, edit paragraphs, replace footers/headers, and change colors.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Overview.Paragraph3
data.value: The page structure is similar to that of bookmarks. When you open the edit page without any documents selected, you will see three main options: create, edit, and the FAQ area.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Overview.HowToSetup.Title
data.value: How to set up a routine?

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Overview.HowToSetup.Desc
data.value: Creating an editing routine is simple. Just click on “create” in the “create” section, then choose the routine function, configure it as desired, and finally give it a name.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Overview.HowToEdit.Desc
data.value: To edit a routine, simply click on the edit button in the edit/application section and when you select a routine, it will be loaded with the previously defined settings.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Overview.HowToApply.Desc
data.value: The application is similar, but you must have at least one document selected and then, in the application section, choose the routine you want to use.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Rewrite.Paragraph1
data.value: The rewrite routine is designed to find text, replace it, and apply a specific style, where you can define a text of up to 200 characters to be found and rewritten.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Rewrite.Paragraph2
data.value: In the settings for this routine, you can define the text styles and where they will be applied. A practical example is for rewriting a template in a specific format.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Paragraph.Paragraph1
data.value: In this function, you can define a default style to be applied to the document's body. You can also control whether the routine is applied to other parts and how it will be applied.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Paragraph.Paragraph2
data.value: Here you can configure the paragraph duplication, which basically duplicates the paragraph with the specified text; in the ignore numbers configuration, all text that does not contain words will be excluded from the routine application.

data.name: Help.Sections.Editor.Paragraph.Paragraph3
data.value: An example of application is if you need to apply a standard style throughout the entire document.

data.name: Help.Sections.Translator.Overview.Paragraph1
data.value: To use the translation system, simply select the files you want to translate on the home or processing page, choose the target language, and click the Translate button.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.Overview.Paragraph1
data.value: Clicking on the gear-shaped button located in the lower right corner opens a section with two areas, one with a list of system notifications, which is generated automatically, and the other with the button to open the system settings.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.Overview.Paragraph2
data.value: Accessing the settings page in the first section, we find the system settings. There, you can change the system theme and the interface language (available in EN, PT, ES, and FR).

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.Overview.Paragraph3
data.value: You can also configure the visibility of high-priority notifications and the number of documents that can be processed simultaneously.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.Overview.Paragraph4
data.value: The number of documents that can be processed at the same time directly affects processing speed. It is recommended for weak computers to leave between 2 and 3, otherwise you can use more.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.Overview.Paragraph5
data.value: The information section in the settings displays relevant information about the system. Finally, in the last section, there is access to the DOT Manager.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.Notifications.Paragraph1
data.value: The system notifies events through three channels: low priority notifications, high priority notifications, and notifications on the device.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.Notifications.Paragraph2
data.value: Low priority notifications: These are available in the settings button section located in the lower right corner. Low priority events are generated by records of changes to system files such as markers/glossaries and changes to settings. The notification list can also be cleared by clicking the clear button.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.Notifications.Paragraph3
data.value: High priority notifications: These are generated by user file manipulation events and are generated at the beginning and end of file processing. They can also be generated when changing notification settings, but are for visual purposes only.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.DOTManager.Paragraph1
data.value: DOT Manager is a DOT support application dedicated to keeping the system up to date, repairing the application, and installing/uninstalling.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.DOTManager.Paragraph2
data.value: The DOT does not depend on it, but it is necessary to bring new features, fix bugs, and improve performance.

data.name: Help.Sections.Settings.DOTManager.Paragraph3
data.value: If you installed DOT with it, you can open it by going to Control Panel > Uninstall a program > DOT (Document Optimizer Tool) > Repair; or by going to Settings and, in the last section, starting DOT Manager.
